title: Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Electric Controls
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 8S/12Q to fewer than 16S/24Q units

program.section_heading: Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Electric Controls – Certificate of Achievement
outcomes: Safety Knowledge and Skills: Acquire and be able to use specific safety knowledge and skills relating to the air conditioning and refrigeration discipline and will be able to apply those skills to specific job requirements.
Installing Servicing and Repairing Systems: Install, service, and repair ACR systems as required by the industry guidelines.
Pressure Testing and Charging Systems: Properly pressure test, evacuate, and charge ACR system.

Attaining Certificates, Degrees, Transferring and Attaining Jobs: Successfully earn a certificate/graduate/transfer to four-year universities and will successfully compete for jobs in which they can apply their knowledge and communicative skills acquired in the air conditioning and refrigeration program.
careers: entry-level heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and controls technician

notes: Program learning outcomes are printed once for the Air Conditioning and Refrigeration department as a whole ('Upon successful completion of the degree or certificate program'); this certificate shares that list, so it is recorded here.

Careers are taken from the department-wide introduction ('Students completing the program may expect to enter industry as an advanced apprentice or entry-level ... controls technician'), which covers the degree and certificates; the certificate's own section names no career beyond 'Recommended for students desiring to enter the air conditioning and refrigeration industry'. Reviewer may wish to confirm.

The section description calls the award 'Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Electrical Controls' while the heading says 'Electric Controls'; the description's content (brazing, domestic refrigerators) does not closely match the listed courses.
The 'Total Units: 13' is recorded as both the certificate total and the block's stated total; the listed course units sum to 13.
